target_customer: Young US consumers and casual investors who want to earn stock rewards on everyday debit spending
problem: Debit card rewards are low and rarely lead to investing; Apollo paid rewards in fractional shares with a chance to win a full share.
business_model: Debit card revenue from interchange, with rewards paid in stock

founders.name: Skyler Aspegren
previous_startups: Deco Base (listed affiliation on YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists Founder @ Deco Base. No education given.

founders.name: Josh Wright
founders.background_notes: YC bio: startup, fintech and iOS app builder, ex Lyft.

competitors.name: Stash (Stock-Back debit card)
competitors.what: Debit card that pays fractional shares of the merchant's stock on qualifying purchases
competitors.traction_then: Reported 500,000 qualifying Stock-Back transactions within about a month of its March 2019 launch
competitors.funding_then: Raised $65M alongside the Stock-Back launch in 2019

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed a card issuing and bank partner stack, ledgering and brokerage of fractional shares, which is standard but regulated fintech integration for three people.

defensibility.rationale: Stock rewards on debit already existed at Stash since 2019 and rely on third-party issuing and brokerage partners, so the idea was easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source describes an incumbent response. Stash already offered the core feature in 2019.

market_need_then: Retail investing boomed in 2020 and 2021 with fractional shares and commission-free apps, which made stock rewards an attractive pitch, though no direct demand metric for Apollo was found.

branding.domain_note: Used withapollo.com, a prefix domain, per the YC and listings

identity.voice_and_tone: Rewards-oriented per the YC tagline, no further source

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community about the brand was found, and searches for the name return Apollo.io and other unrelated companies.

outcome_analysis: Apollo joined YC in Summer 2021 with a three person team and a stock rewards debit card that Stash had already launched in 2019. The YC directory lists it as inactive, but no shutdown report, post-mortem or acquisition was found, so the cause is not public and failure factors are left empty. Public data show only a small seed, so the company likely did not reach a larger round, but that is inferred and not sourced.
notes: Funding rests on CB Insights only (total about $130K, latest round seed, no date). An AngelBacked listing gives a Seed dated 2025-09-24, which conflicts and is not recorded as a round. Crunchbase total is not readable. The withapollo.com host did not resolve in this session so the site state is unknown. Competitor list contains one pre-batch rival; others were not found with dated sources.
